back: Standalone makes Dynamics the system of record. Embedded layers channels, routing, and AI onto an existing CRM or CCaaS that stays the system of record. Keyword: who owns the record?
A representative holds several concurrent conversations as sessions. That is why session and tab templates configure it, not a site map. Keyword: sessions, not pages.
Running simulated interactions through a journey before customers see it — the closest thing to a test suite for a conversational flow. Keyword: test before exposure.
The deployment itself, investigating operational issues proactively rather than waiting for a supervisor to report them. Keyword: it monitors the platform.
Manages the agents as a fleet — which exist, which are published, which channels they serve. Inventory is what separates an estate from a pile. Keyword: fleet view.

front: A promoted environment that routes nothing
back: A solution import carries configuration, not telephony. Channels must be provisioned and numbers acquired and assigned in the target. Keyword: ALM does not move phone numbers.
How much concurrent work a representative can hold — units per channel per conversation. Three chats or one voice call, not both. Keyword: concurrency, in units.
Presence says whether they are available at all; capacity says how much they can take while available. A full queue looks the same either way. Keyword: two different axes.
Without it the customer is anonymous, so the conversation cannot be tied to a record or trusted with account detail. Keyword: anonymous means untrusted.

front: A pre-chat survey is a routing input
back: Its answers become context variables that classification and routing rules act on. It is not merely politeness. Keyword: questions feed the rules.
Asynchronous work arriving as a record — an email or case — routed through the same unified routing as live channels. Keyword: one routing engine for everything.

front: Chat inside a native mobile app
back: The widget cannot cover it. Use the Messaging SDK; the live chat SDK extends the web chat experience. Keyword: SDK where the widget cannot reach.

front: The longest lead time in a voice deployment
back: Phone numbers. They are a regulated real-world resource with country-specific requirements, and they delay more go-lives than configuration does. Keyword: acquire numbers early.
Real-time transcription feeds agent assist; the stored transcript feeds summarisation, sentiment, and quality evaluation. Keyword: no transcript, no AI.

front: The most common complaint about IVR handover
back: The customer repeats an account number they already gave. The fix is passing context across the handover, not shortening the IVR. Keyword: carry the context.

front: Designing context variables is designing routing
back: A rule can only act on a variable that was captured. Decide what to capture before writing the rules. Keyword: capture first, route second.
It matches on what the channel provides. A duplicated contact estate gives ambiguous matches and an unauthenticated channel gives guesses. Keyword: data quality decides accuracy.
It removes patterns as the conversation happens. Transcripts already stored are a separate remediation problem. Keyword: it does not clean history.
Consult adds a second person while the first stays. Transfer hands the conversation over entirely. Context follows in both. Keyword: stay, or hand over.
Preview shows the record before dialling. Progressive dials when a rep is free. Predictive dials ahead of availability. Keyword: increasing talk time, increasing risk.
It dials ahead assuming a proportion will not answer. Too few available reps and the assumption fails. Fix the mode or the staffing, not the list. Keyword: the assumption breaks.

front: Why outbound gets its own workstream
back: So campaign work is routed and measured like inbound rather than existing alongside it unmeasured. Keyword: same machinery, both directions.

front: The gap a headcount forecast hides
back: Skills. Skills-based routing can only reach reps holding the skill, so a shift covering headcount but not skill mix backs queues up while reps sit available. Keyword: forecast the skills.
Generally bidirectional — the centre supplies volume and adherence, the WFM supplies schedules. Decide which system owns the schedule first. Keyword: agree the owner.

front: Copilot with no knowledge sources configured
back: Answers from the model's general training — confidently telling customers things the organisation never published. Keyword: configure the sources.
A representative repeating an answer to a customer must be able to check where it came from. An uncited answer cannot be verified. Keyword: cite or do not use.

front: What the Copilot analytics report is for
back: Turning an impression into a measurement — usage, suggestion acceptance, effect on handling time. Keep-or-reconfigure decisions rest on it. Keyword: measure the assist.
The symptom of trying to enumerate language under classic orchestration. Generative orchestration exists for exactly this. Keyword: stop enumerating phrasings.
DTMF for precise data — account numbers, digits. Speech and NLU for intent. A good voice agent uses both rather than insisting on one. Keyword: keypad for digits.
Passing context in telephony signalling when a call moves between systems, so the customer does not repeat their account number to the human. Keyword: context in the signalling.
Classification enriches the work — variables, identity, intent. Assignment matches it to a queue and a rep. Diagnose which stage first. Keyword: two stages, always.
Work matching no rule is lost silently — conversations nobody answered and nobody knew about. Always define a fallback. Keyword: catch the unmatched.
Every skills-based rule matches zero reps and work falls to overflow. Queues back up while reps sit idle, and more rules make it worse. Keyword: attach skills to people.
For one conversation: which rules evaluated, what matched, where it went. It turns 'routing is broken' into a rule and a condition. Keyword: trace one conversation.
Derives the required skills from the conversation's content instead of requiring them to be set by hand on every item. Keyword: infer the skill.

front: The cost of preferred representative routing
back: It constrains assignment. Heavy use makes queues less fungible and lengthens waits — a trade to make deliberately. Keyword: continuity costs flexibility.
Channels served, session and tab templates, productivity tools, notification templates — assigned to users. Keyword: one deployment, several teams.

front: Where perceived quality actually comes from
back: Session and tab templates — whether the rep starts with the customer's record open or has to go and find it. Keyword: what opens on arrival.
The notification timeout is too short. An unaccepted notification returns the work to the queue. Keyword: timeout causes the bounce.
Substitute live values — customer name, case number — into script text and macros, making a generic procedure specific to this conversation. Keyword: tokens for live values.
Macros invoked from script steps — turning a written procedure into one action. Keyword: automate the repetitive steps.

front: Why link Teams collaboration to the record
back: The discussion is retained with the record instead of being lost in a direct message. Keyword: keep the context with the case.

front: Why knowledge is the highest-leverage content
back: One article improves the human answer, the Copilot answer, and the self-service answer at once. Keyword: write once, three surfaces.
Works on the knowledge base, not conversations — finds gaps where customers ask what no article answers, and drafts updates. Keyword: it closes the loop.
The supervisor's live-conversation actions. Genuinely intrusive, so which are available warrants a deliberate decision. Keyword: configure the intrusion.

front: What the Quality Evaluation agent changes
back: From sampling a few conversations per rep per month to evaluating all of them. The criteria now apply at scale, so they must be right. Keyword: criteria matter more.
Usually not a fault. Real-time reports the current state; historical aggregates completed conversations after processing. Keyword: in-progress counts once.

front: Embedded editor or Power BI Desktop?
back: The embedded editor when the standard report is nearly right. Desktop for deeper change, taking on maintenance through platform updates. Keyword: depth costs maintenance.

front: Embedded reports use Power BI security
back: Not Dataverse row-level security, so what a supervisor sees in a report is not automatically what they see in the app. Keyword: different boundary.
Analytics says how the centre is performing. Application Insights says why, by correlating with the systems behind it. Keyword: performance or cause.
